title: Indonesia 🇮🇩 vs Southeast Asia: 19 rounds, real data. Who wins?
headline: Indonesia vs its *rivals*
description: Indonesia against Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Thailand in 19 rounds: people, money, exports, the rupiah and a quiz on what your $100 is worth. Every number is real World Bank data. Which country should Indonesia face next? Comment your flag.
source: World Bank, World Development Indicators (latest year with data for both countries per round, 2019-2025), data.worldbank.org

segments.text: Indonesia against four neighbours. Nineteen rounds. Real data. Keep score.
One neighbour beats Indonesia by just six dollars. And the last chapter decides everything.
First up. Malaysia. Right next door.
Population. Indonesia has almost eight times more people.
Size of the economy. Indonesia is three times bigger.
Income per person. Malaysia is more than two and a half times richer.
Exports. Eight times fewer people. And Malaysia still sells more. By less than five billion dollars.
Two all. Malaysia holds Indonesia to a draw.
No points here. Just watch the six biggest economies of Southeast Asia since 1990.
In 1990, Indonesia is already number one. Thailand is close behind.
Then the Asian financial crisis hits. In 1998, Thailand takes the lead. For one year.
Indonesia comes back. By 2010, it is more than twice the size of Thailand.
Now watch Vietnam. In 1990, it was the smallest. In 2022, it passes Malaysia.
Today, Indonesia is bigger than Singapore and Thailand combined.
Next up. The Philippines. Five rounds. The score is two all.
Population. Indonesia has almost two and a half times more people.
Income per person. Indonesia wins. By almost nine hundred dollars.
Electricity per person. Indonesia uses about sixty percent more.
Money sent home by workers abroad. The Philippines gets more than twice as much.
Young people without a job. The Philippines wins. Seven percent. Indonesia has thirteen.
Three to two for Indonesia. Overall, five to four.
Two hundred eighty-six million people. This is Indonesia.
Vietnam. One hundred and two million.
Thailand. Seventy-two million.
Malaysia. Thirty-six million.
Put all three together. Indonesia still has more than seventy-six million more people.

props.caption: more people in Indonesia than all three combined

segments.text: Your turn now. No points for the countries. These are for you. Where does one hundred American dollars go further?
Indonesia. There, your hundred dollars feels like three hundred forty-nine. In Thailand, three hundred twenty-six.
Round two. Vietnam or the Philippines?
Vietnam. Three hundred fifty-seven dollars. The Philippines, three hundred two.
Last one. Indonesia or Vietnam?
Vietnam. By just eight dollars. Remember that country. It comes next.
How many did you get? Back to the battle. Indonesia leads five to four.
Vietnam. The fastest grower of all six. Five rounds.
Population. Indonesia has almost three times more people.
Size of the economy. Indonesia is almost three times bigger.
Economic growth. Vietnam grows eight percent a year. Indonesia, five.
Exports. Vietnam sells about fifty percent more to the world.
And income per person. This is the one. Vietnam wins. By six dollars.
Three to two for Vietnam. Overall, seven all.
Now the money itself. In 1990, one dollar bought about eighteen hundred rupiah. Guess what it buys now.
Sixteen thousand five hundred. Almost nine times more. In 1998 alone, the dollar got more than three times more expensive.
Malaysia's ringgit. In 1990, one dollar bought two point seven.
Today, four point three. No points. But the ringgit held on much better.
Final chapter. Thailand. Seven all. Five rounds decide everything.
Population. Indonesia has four times more people.
Tourists before the pandemic. Thailand gets almost two and a half times more.
Income per person. Thailand is almost sixty percent richer.
Two all. Size of the economy. Indonesia is two and a half times bigger.
Last round. Economic growth. Indonesia grows more than twice as fast.
Three to two. Indonesia takes the decider.
Final score. Indonesia ten. The neighbours nine.
Malaysia and Thailand are richer per person. Vietnam is catching up fast. But nobody beats Indonesia's size.
Which country should Indonesia face next?
